summary: Built the full refresh lifecycle: DeviceSnapshot domain struct, state.json persistence, a pure per-device refresh function that preserves last-known data on failure (stale marking), a RefreshCoordinator enforcing max-4-concurrent and one-active-refresh-per-device, a 5s background tick loop driving automatic refresh via managed Tauri state (no unsafe), refresh_device/refresh_all_devices/get_latest_snapshot commands, and the five backend events. 24 new Rust unit tests including a real #[tokio::test] proving the concurrency bound, 123 total passing. Live smoke test confirmed the automatic scheduler end-to-end via state.json, with no UI interaction needed.
completed: domain/snapshot.rs: DeviceSnapshot with stale + lastSuccessfulRefresh fields; failed refreshes carry forward previous metrics/dockerAvailable/containers rather than clearing them.

storage/snapshot_repository.rs: JsonSnapshotRepository for state.json, same atomic-write/corrupted-file-quarantine pattern as config/device repositories; verified the app stays functional after state.json is deleted mid-session.

monitoring/refresh.rs: refresh_device_sync() -- pure, synchronous per-device refresh logic; a failed probe classifies status and stops (stale=true, prior data preserved); a successful probe collects metrics+Docker independently so a Docker failure becomes a warning, not a device failure.

monitoring/concurrency.rs: RefreshCoordinator (Semaphore for max-4-concurrent + in-progress set for one-per-device dedup), with a real #[tokio::test] proving the semaphore actually blocks a 3rd permit under max_concurrent=2 and releases correctly.
monitoring/container_diff.rs: detect_container_changes() -- structural diff powering container://status-changed; deliberately excludes notification-worthiness rules (WU012's job).
monitoring/scheduling.rs: is_due() comparing capturedAt against the device's own interval or the global default.

monitoring/scheduler.rs: refresh_one/refresh_all + a 5s background tick loop started from setup(); looks up RefreshCoordinator via Tauri's managed state (app.state::<T>()) rather than passing borrowed references into spawned tasks, avoiding any unsafe/raw-pointer lifetime workaround. Emits monitoring://refresh-started/-completed, device://snapshot-updated, device://status-changed (only on actual change), container://status-changed (only when non-empty).
commands/monitoring.rs: refresh_device/refresh_all_devices (async, SSH work runs off the async runtime's blocking pool) / get_latest_snapshot.
infrastructure/ssh/error.rs: added SshError::code() mapping to the spec error taxonomy, replacing an ad hoc Debug-string-split.
error.rs: ApplicationError now derives Clone/PartialEq/Deserialize so it round-trips through persisted state.json.
Added tokio (rt/sync/time/macros) as a direct dependency.
src/types/snapshot.ts + src/lib/tauri/monitoring.ts: TypeScript mirror types and command wrappers.
24 new Rust unit tests, 123 total passing. Verified cargo test, cargo build (no warnings), npm run build.

Live smoke test: seeded a device pointing at a closed local port directly into devices.json, launched the app with zero UI interaction, and confirmed via state.json that the background tick loop detected it was due, ran a real ssh.exe probe (genuine ConnectionRefused), classified it Offline, and persisted a snapshot with stale=true -- proving the automatic-refresh path end-to-end without real Pi hardware.

validationCommands.summary: 123/123 unit tests passed (24 new), including a real tokio concurrency test.
Clean build, no warnings, despite adding tokio as a new direct dependency.

validationCommands.command: live smoke test via npm run tauri dev
validationCommands.summary: Automatic background scheduler confirmed end-to-end via state.json contents; no UI click-through needed since this WU has no UI surface.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: A failing/offline device does not stop the scheduler or block other devices' refreshes
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: refresh_all spawns one task per device and swallows individual failures when collecting results ("if let Ok(Ok(snapshot))"); tick() spawns each due device's refresh independently. failed_probe_marks_stale_and_carries_forward_previous_data and friends confirm a single device's failure produces a valid (Offline/stale) snapshot rather than propagating an error that would abort other work.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Manual refresh and automatic refresh both work without freezing the UI
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: refresh_device/refresh_all_devices are async Tauri commands that run the blocking SSH work via spawn_blocking; the automatic path uses the same refresh_one() function via a background tokio task started at setup(), independently confirmed live via the state.json smoke test.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Stale snapshots remain visible with an explicit stale marker and last-refresh timestamp after a failed refresh
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: DeviceSnapshot.stale + capturedAt are always populated; failed_probe_marks_stale_and_carries_forward_previous_data test and the live smoke test's actual state.json output (stale: true, capturedAt populated) both confirm this.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Deleting state.json does not prevent the app from starting
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: app_remains_functional_after_state_json_is_deleted test explicitly deletes the file mid-session and confirms subsequent reads/writes still work; load_all() unconditionally recovers to an empty map on a missing file.

notes: Risk score: 35/100 (medium). Rationale: this is the largest work unit so far -- it introduces a real background async task (the tick loop), a new dependency (tokio), and Tauri-managed shared state (RefreshCoordinator) -- but the concurrency-critical piece is directly tested with a real tokio runtime rather than assumed, and the full automatic-refresh path was verified live end-to-end (not just unit-tested) before considering this done. The main residual risk is the same one carried from WU009/WU010: SYSTEM_METRICS_COMMAND and DOCKER_CONTAINERS_COMMAND still haven't run against real Docker/Raspberry Pi hardware, only against a real-but-closed local port (which exercises the failure path well but not the metrics/Docker success path end-to-end).

container://status-changed emits a structural diff only; deciding which of those changes are actually notification-worthy (dedup key, skip containers already stopped on first discovery) is explicitly the next work unit's scope, matching the plan.

Fixed a design smell during implementation: an earlier draft used a raw pointer + unsafe block to share the RefreshCoordinator across spawned async tasks with a non-'static borrow. Replaced with Tauri's app.state::<T>() managed-state lookup, which is fully safe and the idiomatic pattern -- worth remembering as the default approach for any future scheduler-adjacent shared state, rather than reaching for unsafe.

The live smoke test also surfaced a testing-environment fact worth remembering for future manual verification: Tauri's app_config_dir() resolves to %APPDATA% (Roaming), while the log plugin's app_log_dir() resolves to %LOCALAPPDATA% -- they are not the same directory on Windows.
